To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) asthma knowledge does not have a major impact on asthma management, 2) asthma education programs can be effective in improving asthma management and 3) the effectiveness of education programs is influenced by the patients' motivation to participate in the program.

knowledge of asthma is a necessary but not sufficient condition for optimal asthma management; knowledge of asthma is not directly linked to the implementation of behavioural changes in everyday life but it has an important indirect effect; the relevance of asthma education programs is to be evaluated in terms of their impact on the patients' self-management, compliance, and coping.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to promote the self-management of patients suffering from asthma and how to identify those patients with little knowledge about their disease.
the question of what knowledge about asthma means for patients' ability to manage their own disease.
the question whether and how knowledge of the disease can help patients to manage their asthma in the long term and how it is possible to impart such knowledge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
knowledge about asthma does have an indirect effect on self-management.
knowledge about asthma is a necessary, but not a sufficient, prerequisite for optimal asthma care.
knowledge about asthma is not a prerequisite for self-management of the disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
asthma knowledge is an important factor in the management of asthma, but that it is not sufficient to achieve optimal asthma management.
knowledge about asthma is not sufficient to enable self-management.
asthma education programs should be designed in such a way that they address both knowledge and behaviour.
The main takeaway from our work is that
knowledge about asthma is an essential component of asthma education, but it is not sufficient for patients} self-management.
knowledge about asthma alone is not enough to improve self-management of asthma.
asthma knowledge is only one factor among many which influence the ability of patients and their families to self-manage asthma.
